title: feat: add `size` prop to ConnectWalletButton
body:
## Summary

The `ConnectWalletButton` currently has no built-in size variants. Consumers must override sizing entirely through `className`. Adding a first-class `size` prop improves the copy-paste ergonomics.

## Implementation Steps

1. Open `src/components/wallet/ConnectWalletButton.tsx`.
2. Add a `size` prop typed as `'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'` with a default of `'md'`.
3. Map each size to a `data-size` attribute on the `<button>` element (e.g. `data-size="sm"`). Do **not** apply inline styles — consumers target the attribute in their own CSS or Tailwind variants.
4. Export the `Size` type from `src/types/index.ts` so consumers can import it.
5. Update the JSDoc comment on the component.
6. Add a test case in `tests/components.test.tsx` asserting the `data-size` attribute is set correctly for each variant.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] `size` prop accepted and forwarded as `data-size` attribute.
- [ ] Type exported from `src/types/index.ts`.
- [ ] At least three test cases (one per size) pass.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test` all green.

title: feat: add `truncateLength` prop to CopyableAddress
body:
## Summary

`CopyableAddress` currently hard-codes a truncation of 6 leading + 4 trailing characters. Different UI contexts need different lengths.

## Implementation Steps

1. Open `src/components/common/CopyableAddress.tsx`.
2. Replace the hard-coded slice values with a `truncateLength` prop typed as `{ leading: number; trailing: number }` defaulting to `{ leading: 6, trailing: 4 }`.
3. The `truncate` boolean prop should remain; when `false`, `truncateLength` is ignored.
4. Update the component's JSDoc.
5. Add tests covering custom `truncateLength` values.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] `truncateLength` prop accepted with correct defaults.
- [ ] Existing `truncate={false}` behaviour unchanged.
- [ ] Tests pass.
- [ ] No TypeScript errors.

title: feat: implement `useHorizonSSE` hook for real-time transaction streaming
body:
## Summary

`useTransactions` currently does a one-shot Horizon fetch. Horizon supports Server-Sent Events (SSE) for streaming new transactions in real time. This hook should wrap that capability.

## Implementation Steps

1. Create `src/hooks/useHorizonSSE.ts`.
2. Signature: `useHorizonSSE(publicKey: string | null, network: StellarNetwork, onRecord: (tx: TransactionRecord) => void): { close: () => void }`.
3. Use `Horizon.Server.transactions().forAccount(publicKey).cursor('now').stream({ onmessage, onerror })` from `@stellar/stellar-sdk`.
4. Call `close()` in the `useEffect` cleanup to prevent memory leaks.
5. Map the raw Horizon record to `TransactionRecord` using the same mapping logic as `useTransactions`.
6. Export from `src/index.ts`.
7. Write a unit test using `vi.mock('@stellar/stellar-sdk')` to simulate the stream emitting one record and verify `onRecord` is called.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Hook opens SSE stream on mount and closes on unmount.
- [ ] `onRecord` called with correctly typed `TransactionRecord`.
- [ ] No memory leaks (cleanup verified in test).
- [ ] TypeScript strict mode passes.

title: feat: add `ReceiveAddressQR` component using `qrcode.react`
body:
## Summary

Users need a way to display their Stellar public key as a QR code for easy scanning. This component wraps `qrcode.react` and adds a copy button.

## Implementation Steps

1. Discuss adding `qrcode.react` as a dependency in this issue before merging — it must be approved by a maintainer.
2. Create `src/components/common/ReceiveAddressQR.tsx`.
3. Props: `address: string`, `size?: number` (default `200`), `className?: string`, `showCopyButton?: boolean` (default `true`).
4. Render `<QRCodeSVG value={address} size={size} />` from `qrcode.react`.
5. If `showCopyButton` is true, render a `<CopyableAddress address={address} />` below the QR code.
6. Wrap the whole component in a `<figure>` with `<figcaption>` showing the truncated address for screen readers.
7. Export from `src/index.ts`.
8. Write tests: renders SVG element; renders copy button when `showCopyButton=true`; hides copy button when `false`.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] QR code renders as SVG.
- [ ] Copy button conditionally rendered.
- [ ] Accessible `<figure>` / `<figcaption>` structure.
- [ ] Dependency approved and pinned to exact version.
- [ ] Tests pass.

title: feat: add `TransactionFilters` component for filtering history by type and asset
body:
## Summary

`TransactionHistory` renders a flat list with no filtering. A companion `TransactionFilters` component should provide controlled filter state that consumers can wire up.

## Implementation Steps

1. Create `src/components/transaction/TransactionFilters.tsx`.
2. Props:
   - `types: TransactionRecord['type'][]` — available type options.
   - `assets: string[]` — available asset codes.
   - `value: { types: TransactionRecord['type'][]; asset: string | null }` — controlled value.
   - `onChange: (filters: typeof value) => void`.
   - `className?: string`.
3. Render a group of toggle buttons for `types` and a `<select>` for `asset`. Use Radix UI `ToggleGroup` for the type buttons.
4. All interactive elements must have visible labels and keyboard support.
5. Export from `src/index.ts`.
6. Export the `TransactionFilters` value type as `TransactionFilterState` from `src/types/index.ts`.
7. Write tests: toggling a type calls `onChange` with updated array; selecting an asset calls `onChange`.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Fully controlled component (no internal state).
- [ ] Radix UI `ToggleGroup` used for type filters.
- [ ] `TransactionFilterState` type exported.
- [ ] Keyboard accessible.
- [ ] Tests pass.

title: feat: add `xBull` wallet adapter to `WalletProvider`
body:
## Summary

`WalletProvider` currently only has a stub for Freighter. xBull is a popular Stellar wallet and should be supported via the same adapter pattern.

## Implementation Steps

1. Create `src/utils/walletAdapters.ts` defining a `WalletAdapter` interface:
   ```ts
   interface WalletAdapter {
     name: string;
     isAvailable: () => boolean;
     getPublicKey: () => Promise<string>;
     signTransaction: (xdr: string) => Promise<string>;
   }
   ```
2. Implement `FreighterAdapter` and `XBullAdapter` in the same file, each satisfying `WalletAdapter`.
3. Refactor `WalletProvider` to accept an `adapters?: WalletAdapter[]` prop (default: `[FreighterAdapter, XBullAdapter]`). The `connect()` function should try adapters in order and use the first available one.
4. Expose `activeAdapter: WalletAdapter | null` on the context value.
5. Export `WalletAdapter`, `FreighterAdapter`, `XBullAdapter` from `src/index.ts`.
6. Write unit tests mocking `window.freighter` and `window.xBullSDK`.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] `WalletAdapter` interface defined and exported.
- [ ] Both adapters implemented.
- [ ] `WalletProvider` uses adapter list.
- [ ] `activeAdapter` exposed on context.
- [ ] Tests pass with mocked globals.

title: feat: implement `SEP24Dialog` component for hosted deposit/withdrawal flows
body:
## Summary

[SEP-24](https://github.com/stellar/stellar-protocol/blob/master/ecosystem/sep-0024.md) defines the interactive anchor deposit and withdrawal protocol. This is the most complex component in the kit — it opens an anchor's hosted iframe flow inside a Radix UI `Dialog`.

## Background

SEP-24 flow:
1. Fetch the anchor's `stellar.toml` to discover the `TRANSFER_SERVER_SEP0024` URL.
2. Call `GET /info` to list supported assets and operations.
3. Call `POST /transactions/deposit/interactive` or `POST /transactions/withdraw/interactive` with a JWT (obtained via SEP-10).
4. Open the returned `url` in an iframe inside a modal.
5. Poll `GET /transaction?id=` until the transaction reaches a terminal state (`completed`, `error`, `refunded`).

## Implementation Steps

1. Create `src/components/transaction/SEP24Dialog.tsx`.
2. Props:
   - `anchorDomain: string` — e.g. `"myanchor.io"`.
   - `operation: 'deposit' | 'withdraw'`.
   - `assetCode: string`.
   - `jwt: string` — SEP-10 JWT; obtaining it is out of scope for this component.
   - `onSuccess: (transactionId: string) => void`.
   - `onError: (error: Error) => void`.
   - `onClose: () => void`.
   - `open: boolean`.
   - `className?: string`.
3. Use `@stellar/stellar-sdk`'s `StellarToml.Resolver.resolve()` to fetch the TOML.
4. Use Radix UI `Dialog.Root / Dialog.Content` for the modal shell.
5. Render the anchor URL in an `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-forms allow-popups" />` — the `sandbox` attribute is mandatory for security.
6. Implement polling with `setInterval` (clear on unmount). Poll every 5 seconds.
7. Create `src/hooks/useSEP24Transaction.ts` to encapsulate the polling logic.
8. Export `SEP24Dialog` and `useSEP24Transaction` from `src/index.ts`.
9. Write tests:
   - Renders `Dialog` when `open=true`.
   - Does not render iframe when `open=false`.
   - Calls `onSuccess` when polling returns `completed`.
   - Calls `onError` when polling returns `error`.

## Security Considerations

- Always use `sandbox` on the iframe.
- Never pass the JWT as a URL query parameter — use the anchor's `POST` endpoint.
- Validate that the polled transaction ID matches the one returned by the initial POST.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] TOML resolution implemented.
- [ ] Radix UI Dialog used for modal shell.
- [ ] Iframe rendered with correct `sandbox` attributes.
- [ ] Polling implemented in `useSEP24Transaction` hook.
- [ ] `onSuccess` / `onError` / `onClose` callbacks all wired up.
- [ ] Security considerations addressed.
- [ ] All tests pass.
- [ ] No TypeScript errors in strict mode.

title: docs: add Storybook stories for all existing components
body:
## Summary

There are currently no interactive component previews. Adding Storybook stories makes it easy for contributors and consumers to explore components without setting up a full app.

## Implementation Steps

1. Install Storybook: `npx storybook@latest init` — choose the Vite + React builder. Discuss the dependency additions in this issue before merging.
2. Create stories under `src/components/**/*.stories.tsx` (co-located with components).
3. Required stories:
   - `ConnectWalletButton` — Default, Connecting, Connected states.
   - `CopyableAddress` — Truncated, Full.
   - `AssetDisplay` — Native XLM, Custom asset with issuer shown.
   - `AssetBalanceList` — Empty, Multiple assets.
   - `TransactionStatusBadge` — Pending, Success, Failed.
   - `TransactionHistory` — Loading, Empty, Populated.
   - `SendPaymentForm` — Default.
4. Add a `storybook` and `build-storybook` script to `package.json`.
5. Update `CONTRIBUTING.md` with instructions for running Storybook locally.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Storybook initialised and running (`npm run storybook`).
- [ ] All listed stories created.
- [ ] `CONTRIBUTING.md` updated.
- [ ] No TypeScript errors in story files.

title: feat: add `useStellarAccount` polling interval option and manual refetch
body:
## Summary

`useStellarAccount` fetches once on mount. For live balance displays, consumers need either automatic polling or a manual refetch trigger. The hook already exposes `refetch` but has no auto-poll capability.

## Implementation Steps

1. Open `src/hooks/useStellarAccount.ts`.
2. Add an optional `pollingInterval?: number` parameter (milliseconds). When provided and `> 0`, set up a `setInterval` that calls `refetch` on the given interval. Clear the interval on unmount.
3. The `refetch` function returned by the hook must remain stable across renders (wrap in `useCallback`).
4. Add an `isStale: boolean` field to the return type — set to `true` after the first successful fetch and reset to `false` while a new fetch is in flight.
5. Export the updated return type as `UseStellarAccountResult` from `src/types/index.ts`.
6. Write tests:
   - `pollingInterval` of 1000ms triggers a second fetch after 1 second (use `vi.useFakeTimers()`).
   - Interval is cleared when the component unmounts.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] `pollingInterval` option implemented.
- [ ] `isStale` field added to return type.
- [ ] `refetch` is referentially stable.
- [ ] `UseStellarAccountResult` exported from types.
- [ ] Tests use fake timers and pass.
- [ ] No TypeScript errors.
